**4B.4 Research Note**

Overall judgment: **No**. The 2024 record shows limited, reactive gestures toward oversight, but not a genuine pattern of strengthening institutions that could constrain Sharif. The clearest positives are an inquiry commission on judicial intimidation and the ombudsman’s complaint-handling work. The clearest negatives are the 26th Amendment’s judicial changes, media/platform restrictions, and repeated repression of dissent and protest.

- [Pakistan to investigate army’s meddling in judiciary, law minister says](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/3/28/pakistan-to-investigate-armys-meddling-in-judiciary-law-minister-says) - **Reuters via Al Jazeera**, 2024-03-28. Claim: After six High Court judges alleged ISI intimidation in politically sensitive cases, the Sharif government said it would form an inquiry commission. This is the strongest positive evidence for oversight, but it is reactive and does not show durable court-strengthening. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 3B.4.

- [Mohtasib resolves 193,028 complaints, provides relief of Rs 48.98 billion](https://president.gov.pk/mohtasib-resolves-193028-complaints-provides-relief-of-rs-4898-billion-2) - **President of Pakistan**, 2024-02-07. Claim: The federal ombudsman handled a large volume of complaints and provided relief, showing complaint-handling infrastructure remained active in 2024. This supports a narrow oversight-positive reading, but it is inherited institutional capacity rather than Sharif-driven empowerment. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 3B.4.

- [HRW World Report 2024: Pakistan](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/pakistan) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024. Claim: HRW reported that, after prison-health reporting, Sharif ordered sanitation and healthcare measures in Lahore Central Prison and promised wider prison reforms. This is a limited oversight-related positive, but it is reactive and prison-specific rather than a broad strengthening of accountability bodies. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 3B.4, 3B.7.

- [Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) - **The Guardian**, 2024-10-21. Claim: The 26th Amendment changed senior-judge appointment rules in ways critics said weakened judicial independence, and it passed amid allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs. This is strong negative evidence against strengthening independent courts. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 4B.2, 3B.4.

- [Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024-01-11. Claim: HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, the opposition, and NGOs, with media pressure and weak safeguards deepening self-censorship. This cuts directly against strengthening oversight institutions or allowing them to function independently. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8.

- [Pakistan: Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-02-08. Claim: The election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown chilled expression, assembly, and monitoring during a politically sensitive moment. While carried out under the caretaker environment, it still weighs against a broader claim that Sharif’s political order strengthened independent scrutiny. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 4B.2, 4B.3.

- [The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-09-09. Claim: Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded powers to restrict gatherings. That points to entrenchment through control, not empowerment of oversight or civic checks. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8.

- [Pakistan Government Intensifies Crackdown on Political Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024-10-09. Claim: HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against PTI protesters, including peaceful demonstrators. This is direct evidence against any claim that Sharif strengthened institutions that could constrain coercive power. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9.

- [Dangerous digital crackdown](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024-12-12. Claim: HRW said internet shutdowns and VPN restrictions had become default policing tools, while a PECA-linked body would expand prosecution powers. This is strong evidence against independent oversight, especially in the media/digital sphere. **QIDs:** 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8.

**Search gap**

- I found **no solid 2024 evidence** that Sharif materially strengthened local governments, audit bodies, or parliament as independent checks on his own power.
- The positive evidence is narrow and mostly reactive. The negative evidence is broader, especially around courts, media, protest, and digital oversight.
